scene.label: Act 1, Scene 3
scene.title: SCENE III. A Room in the Palace

lines.text: Why, cousin, why, Rosalind! Cupid have mercy! Not a word?
lines.plainText: Why cousin why Rosalind Cupid have mercy Not a word

lines.text: Not one to throw at a dog.
lines.plainText: Not one to throw at a dog

lines.text: No, thy words are too precious to be cast away upon curs. Throw some of them at me. Come, lame me with reasons.
lines.plainText: No thy words are too precious to be cast away upon curs Throw some of them at me Come lame me with reasons

lines.text: Then there were two cousins laid up, when the one should be lamed with reasons and the other mad without any.
lines.plainText: Then there were two cousins laid up when the one should be lamed with reasons and the other mad without any

lines.text: But is all this for your father?
lines.plainText: But is all this for your father

lines.text: No, some of it is for my child's father. O, how full of briers is this working-day world!
lines.plainText: No some of it is for my child's father O how full of briers is this workingday world

lines.text: They are but burs, cousin, thrown upon thee in holiday foolery. If we walk not in the trodden paths, our very petticoats will catch them.
lines.plainText: They are but burs cousin thrown upon thee in holiday foolery If we walk not in the trodden paths our very petticoats will catch them

lines.text: I could shake them off my coat; these burs are in my heart.
lines.plainText: I could shake them off my coat these burs are in my heart

lines.text: Hem them away.
lines.plainText: Hem them away

lines.text: I would try, if I could cry "hem" and have him.
lines.plainText: I would try if I could cry hem and have him

lines.text: Come, come, wrestle with thy affections.
lines.plainText: Come come wrestle with thy affections

lines.text: O, they take the part of a better wrestler than myself.
lines.plainText: O they take the part of a better wrestler than myself

lines.text: O, a good wish upon you! You will try in time, in despite of a fall. But turning these jests out of service, let us talk in good earnest. Is it possible on such a sudden you should fall into so strong a liking with old Sir Rowland's youngest son?
lines.plainText: O a good wish upon you You will try in time in despite of a fall But turning these jests out of service let us talk in good earnest Is it possible on such a sudden you should fall into so strong a liking with old Sir Rowland's youngest son

lines.text: The Duke my father loved his father dearly.
lines.plainText: The Duke my father loved his father dearly

lines.text: Doth it therefore ensue that you should love his son dearly? By this kind of chase I should hate him, for my father hated his father dearly; yet I hate not Orlando.
lines.plainText: Doth it therefore ensue that you should love his son dearly By this kind of chase I should hate him for my father hated his father dearly yet I hate not Orlando

lines.text: No, faith, hate him not, for my sake.
lines.plainText: No faith hate him not for my sake

lines.text: Why should I not? Doth he not deserve well?
lines.plainText: Why should I not Doth he not deserve well

lines.text: Let me love him for that, and do you love him because I do.—Look, here comes the Duke.
lines.plainText: Let me love him for that and do you love him because I doLook here comes the Duke

lines.text: With his eyes full of anger.
lines.plainText: With his eyes full of anger

lines.text: Mistress, dispatch you with your safest haste,
lines.plainText: Mistress dispatch you with your safest haste

lines.text: And get you from our court.
lines.plainText: And get you from our court

lines.text: Me, uncle?
lines.plainText: Me uncle

lines.text: You, cousin.
lines.plainText: You cousin

lines.text: Within these ten days if that thou be'st found
lines.plainText: Within these ten days if that thou be'st found

lines.text: So near our public court as twenty miles,
lines.plainText: So near our public court as twenty miles

lines.text: Thou diest for it.
lines.plainText: Thou diest for it

lines.text: I do beseech your Grace,
lines.plainText: I do beseech your Grace

lines.text: Let me the knowledge of my fault bear with me.
lines.plainText: Let me the knowledge of my fault bear with me

lines.text: If with myself I hold intelligence,
lines.plainText: If with myself I hold intelligence

lines.text: Or have acquaintance with mine own desires,
lines.plainText: Or have acquaintance with mine own desires

lines.text: If that I do not dream, or be not frantic—
lines.plainText: If that I do not dream or be not frantic

lines.text: As I do trust I am not—then, dear uncle,
lines.plainText: As I do trust I am notthen dear uncle

lines.text: Never so much as in a thought unborn
lines.plainText: Never so much as in a thought unborn

lines.text: Did I offend your Highness.
lines.plainText: Did I offend your Highness

lines.text: Thus do all traitors.
lines.plainText: Thus do all traitors

lines.text: If their purgation did consist in words,
lines.plainText: If their purgation did consist in words

lines.text: They are as innocent as grace itself.
lines.plainText: They are as innocent as grace itself

lines.text: Let it suffice thee that I trust thee not.
lines.plainText: Let it suffice thee that I trust thee not

lines.text: Yet your mistrust cannot make me a traitor.
lines.plainText: Yet your mistrust cannot make me a traitor

lines.text: Tell me whereon the likelihood depends.
lines.plainText: Tell me whereon the likelihood depends

lines.text: Thou art thy father's daughter, there's enough.
lines.plainText: Thou art thy father's daughter there's enough

lines.text: So was I when your highness took his dukedom;
lines.plainText: So was I when your highness took his dukedom

lines.text: So was I when your highness banished him.
lines.plainText: So was I when your highness banished him

lines.text: Treason is not inherited, my lord,
lines.plainText: Treason is not inherited my lord

lines.text: Or, if we did derive it from our friends,
lines.plainText: Or if we did derive it from our friends

lines.text: What's that to me? My father was no traitor.
lines.plainText: What's that to me My father was no traitor

lines.text: Then, good my liege, mistake me not so much
lines.plainText: Then good my liege mistake me not so much

lines.text: To think my poverty is treacherous.
lines.plainText: To think my poverty is treacherous

lines.text: Dear sovereign, hear me speak.
lines.plainText: Dear sovereign hear me speak

lines.text: Ay, Celia, we stayed her for your sake,
lines.plainText: Ay Celia we stayed her for your sake

lines.text: Else had she with her father ranged along.
lines.plainText: Else had she with her father ranged along

lines.text: I did not then entreat to have her stay;
lines.plainText: I did not then entreat to have her stay

lines.text: It was your pleasure and your own remorse.
lines.plainText: It was your pleasure and your own remorse

lines.text: I was too young that time to value her,
lines.plainText: I was too young that time to value her

lines.text: But now I know her. If she be a traitor,
lines.plainText: But now I know her If she be a traitor

lines.text: Why, so am I. We still have slept together,
lines.plainText: Why so am I We still have slept together

lines.text: Rose at an instant, learned, played, ate together,
lines.plainText: Rose at an instant learned played ate together

lines.text: And wheresoe'er we went, like Juno's swans,
lines.plainText: And wheresoe'er we went like Juno's swans

lines.text: Still we went coupled and inseparable.
lines.plainText: Still we went coupled and inseparable

lines.text: She is too subtle for thee, and her smoothness,
lines.plainText: She is too subtle for thee and her smoothness

lines.text: Her very silence, and her patience
lines.plainText: Her very silence and her patience

lines.text: Speak to the people, and they pity her.
lines.plainText: Speak to the people and they pity her

lines.text: Thou art a fool. She robs thee of thy name,
lines.plainText: Thou art a fool She robs thee of thy name

lines.text: And thou wilt show more bright and seem more virtuous
lines.plainText: And thou wilt show more bright and seem more virtuous

lines.text: When she is gone. Then open not thy lips.
lines.plainText: When she is gone Then open not thy lips

lines.text: Firm and irrevocable is my doom
lines.plainText: Firm and irrevocable is my doom

lines.text: Which I have passed upon her. She is banished.
lines.plainText: Which I have passed upon her She is banished

lines.text: Pronounce that sentence then on me, my liege.
lines.plainText: Pronounce that sentence then on me my liege

lines.text: I cannot live out of her company.
lines.plainText: I cannot live out of her company

lines.text: You are a fool. You, niece, provide yourself.
lines.plainText: You are a fool You niece provide yourself

lines.text: If you outstay the time, upon mine honour
lines.plainText: If you outstay the time upon mine honour

lines.text: And in the greatness of my word, you die.
lines.plainText: And in the greatness of my word you die

lines.text: O my poor Rosalind, whither wilt thou go?
lines.plainText: O my poor Rosalind whither wilt thou go

lines.text: Wilt thou change fathers? I will give thee mine.
lines.plainText: Wilt thou change fathers I will give thee mine

lines.text: I charge thee, be not thou more grieved than I am.
lines.plainText: I charge thee be not thou more grieved than I am

lines.text: I have more cause.
lines.plainText: I have more cause

lines.text: Thou hast not, cousin.
lines.plainText: Thou hast not cousin

lines.text: Prithee be cheerful. Know'st thou not the Duke
lines.plainText: Prithee be cheerful Know'st thou not the Duke

lines.text: Hath banished me, his daughter?
lines.plainText: Hath banished me his daughter

lines.text: That he hath not.
lines.plainText: That he hath not

lines.text: No, hath not? Rosalind lacks then the love
lines.plainText: No hath not Rosalind lacks then the love

lines.text: Which teacheth thee that thou and I am one.
lines.plainText: Which teacheth thee that thou and I am one

lines.text: Shall we be sundered? Shall we part, sweet girl?
lines.plainText: Shall we be sundered Shall we part sweet girl

lines.text: No, let my father seek another heir.
lines.plainText: No let my father seek another heir

lines.text: Therefore devise with me how we may fly,
lines.plainText: Therefore devise with me how we may fly

lines.text: Whither to go, and what to bear with us,
lines.plainText: Whither to go and what to bear with us

lines.text: And do not seek to take your change upon you,
lines.plainText: And do not seek to take your change upon you

lines.text: To bear your griefs yourself and leave me out.
lines.plainText: To bear your griefs yourself and leave me out

lines.text: For, by this heaven, now at our sorrows pale,
lines.plainText: For by this heaven now at our sorrows pale

lines.text: Say what thou canst, I'll go along with thee.
lines.plainText: Say what thou canst I'll go along with thee

lines.text: Why, whither shall we go?
lines.plainText: Why whither shall we go

lines.text: To seek my uncle in the Forest of Arden.
lines.plainText: To seek my uncle in the Forest of Arden

lines.text: Alas, what danger will it be to us,
lines.plainText: Alas what danger will it be to us

lines.text: Maids as we are, to travel forth so far?
lines.plainText: Maids as we are to travel forth so far

lines.text: Beauty provoketh thieves sooner than gold.
lines.plainText: Beauty provoketh thieves sooner than gold

lines.text: I'll put myself in poor and mean attire,
lines.plainText: I'll put myself in poor and mean attire

lines.text: And with a kind of umber smirch my face.
lines.plainText: And with a kind of umber smirch my face

lines.text: The like do you; so shall we pass along
lines.plainText: The like do you so shall we pass along

lines.text: And never stir assailants.
lines.plainText: And never stir assailants

lines.text: Were it not better,
lines.plainText: Were it not better

lines.text: Because that I am more than common tall,
lines.plainText: Because that I am more than common tall

lines.text: That I did suit me all points like a man?
lines.plainText: That I did suit me all points like a man

lines.text: A gallant curtal-axe upon my thigh,
lines.plainText: A gallant curtalaxe upon my thigh

lines.text: A boar-spear in my hand, and in my heart
lines.plainText: A boarspear in my hand and in my heart

lines.text: Lie there what hidden woman's fear there will,
lines.plainText: Lie there what hidden woman's fear there will

lines.text: We'll have a swashing and a martial outside,
lines.plainText: We'll have a swashing and a martial outside

lines.text: As many other mannish cowards have
lines.plainText: As many other mannish cowards have

lines.text: That do outface it with their semblances.
lines.plainText: That do outface it with their semblances

lines.text: What shall I call thee when thou art a man?
lines.plainText: What shall I call thee when thou art a man

lines.text: I'll have no worse a name than Jove's own page,
lines.plainText: I'll have no worse a name than Jove's own page

lines.text: And therefore look you call me Ganymede.
lines.plainText: And therefore look you call me Ganymede

lines.text: But what will you be called?
lines.plainText: But what will you be called

lines.text: Something that hath a reference to my state:
lines.plainText: Something that hath a reference to my state

lines.text: No longer Celia, but Aliena.
lines.plainText: No longer Celia but Aliena

lines.text: But, cousin, what if we assayed to steal
lines.plainText: But cousin what if we assayed to steal

lines.text: The clownish fool out of your father's court?
lines.plainText: The clownish fool out of your father's court

lines.text: Would he not be a comfort to our travel?
lines.plainText: Would he not be a comfort to our travel

lines.text: He'll go along o'er the wide world with me.
lines.plainText: He'll go along o'er the wide world with me

lines.text: Leave me alone to woo him. Let's away,
lines.plainText: Leave me alone to woo him Let's away

lines.text: And get our jewels and our wealth together,
lines.plainText: And get our jewels and our wealth together

lines.text: Devise the fittest time and safest way
lines.plainText: Devise the fittest time and safest way

lines.text: To hide us from pursuit that will be made
lines.plainText: To hide us from pursuit that will be made

lines.text: After my flight. Now go we in content
lines.plainText: After my flight Now go we in content

lines.text: To liberty, and not to banishment.
lines.plainText: To liberty and not to banishment
